notes:
Product/Business overview: KiteAnchor builds product analytics SDK + in-app assistant for B2B SaaS products. Primary value prop is contextual guidance inside product and deep semantic search across event+session data.

Engagement summary: did 4-week Hosted API trial (Jan 20 - Feb 17). Goal: validate latency, cost, and correctness for in-app assistant + reranking pipeline before committing to Dedicated capacity. AE/SE-led POC. Several demo sessions, one live run with ~50 internal users.

Hosted trial observations (quantitative):
- Traffic observed during trial: avg QPS ~28 (steady-state), peak sustained QPS 95 during internal load test. Typical concurrency observed: 8-12 active sessions, bursts up to 48.
- Token mix: ~35% short queries (<50 tokens), ~50% medium (50-500 tokens), ~15% long (>500 tokens) due to session context re-sends. Average request: 120 input tokens / 220 output tokens.
- Latency: p50 ~85ms, p95 ~220ms on redwood-hosted baseline model; embeddings requests p95 ~40ms.
- Cost signals: generated cost per heavy-chat session higher than expected; team is sensitive to per-token cost for long-form explanations and multi-turn contexts.

Requirements for Dedicated sizing:
- Target production SLA: p95 latency <250ms for chat flows, throughput target 400 QPS steady-state at launch+scale; peak bursts 800 QPS for marketing events.
- Expected concurrency for launch (MVP): 40 concurrent active users; growth plan -> 200 concurrent within 12 months.
- KV/prefix cache strategy: reuse session KV where possible to reduce generation tokens by ~20% (SE recommended).
- Model preference: prefer open-model variants verified by Redwood (cost vs perf tradeoff). They want routing policy to favor cheaper variants for non-critical queries and fallback to stronger models for core assistant paths.

Traffic forecast (customer-provided, validated by SE):
- Month 0 (post-launch): avg QPS 40, concurrency 30.
- Month 3: avg QPS 120, concurrency 90.
- Month 6: avg QPS 220, concurrency 160.
- Month 12: avg QPS 420, concurrency 300.
Assumed token mix remains similar; plan includes 15% reduction in tokens after applying prefix caching and prompt compacting.

Sizing recommendation (initial Dedicated commit draft):
- Minimum reserved pool: 4x A100-equivalent instances (or optimized GPU types recommended by Redwood) with autoscale buffer of +2 instances for bursts.
- Workload partitioning: separate pools for embeddings vs generation to avoid head-of-line blocking; embedding pool can be smaller but must handle batched traffic.
- Expected cost delta vs hosted: committed monthly capacity reduces unit cost by ~35% for their token profile (SE preliminary estimate).

Security/compliance notes:
- Customer requires SOC2 attestation, SSO via SAML (Okta), KMS integration for key wrapping, and 12-month audit log retention. Data residency requirement: US-only for PII-related artifacts. Legal has a few items on subprocessor lists.

Conversations and quotes:
- Pricing: initial quote shared (drive link). Finance asked for 3-tier pricing: dev/staging, production, peak buffer. They are evaluating a 12-month reserved contract vs 6-month pilot.
- SE notes: recommend running 48-hour soak with Dedicated staging pool configured to expected concurrency to validate autoscaler and KV cache behavior before prod cutover.

Next actions (short):
